label: Veterinary clinic
about: Caring veterinary clinic for dogs, cats and small pets: check-ups, vaccinations, surgery and emergencies.
booking_question: What's your pet's name and species, and what's the appointment for? (e.g. vaccination for Luna, our cat)

faqs.q: Do you see emergencies? | emergency vet | out of hours | 24 hours
faqs.a: Yes. During opening hours, come straight in or call us. Out of hours, call our emergency number.

faqs.q: What animals do you treat? | do you see rabbits | exotic | birds | reptiles
faqs.a: We treat dogs, cats, rabbits and other small pets. For reptiles and birds, call us first and we'll tell you if we can help.

faqs.q: When should my puppy or kitten be vaccinated? | puppy vaccines | kitten vaccines | first vaccination
faqs.a: Usually from 6 to 8 weeks old, with boosters a few weeks later. Book a first visit and we'll set up the full plan.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment? | walk in
faqs.a: Appointments are best so you don't wait, but we always see emergencies straight away.

faqs.q: Can I pay in instalments? | payment plan | pet insurance | insurance
faqs.a: We accept most pet insurance and can talk about payment plans for bigger treatments. Ask us at reception.

faqs.q: Should I fast my pet before surgery? | before the operation | fasting
faqs.a: Usually no food from 10 pm the night before; water is fine. We'll give you exact instructions when you book.

emergencies.keywords: ate chocolate | ate poison | poisoned | ate rat poison | ate grapes | ate raisins | ate xylitol | swallowed | not breathing | can't breathe | struggling to breathe | collapsed | seizure | fitting | hit by a car | bleeding | heatstroke | bloated | trying to vomit | envenenado
emergencies.message: This could be an emergency. Please call us now so we can tell you what to do and get ready for you. Don't try to make your pet vomit unless a vet tells you to. If they ate something, bring the packaging or a sample with you.
